Dot product — east, north, and northeast

The dot product as directional similarity, seen before it is calculated. You travel east at 1 mph and a friend travels north: the two directions share nothing, so the similarity gauge sits empty — and only then does the component arithmetic produce the zero that says the same thing. The friend turns northeast, still 1 mph, the gauge fills most of the way, and the calculation puts √2/2 ≈ 0.707 on it. The clip closes on the limit of that reading: u·v = ∥u∥∥v∥cos θ collapses to cos θ only because both magnitudes are 1 — so what happens when the vectors are different sizes? That question is the hook for the follow-up clip.

Pause points (each sits on a 2s hold):

  • no commonality — 14.0s
  • east dot north — 24.78s
  • some commonality — 33.22s
  • east dot northeast — 46.56s
  • unit vectors only — 56.44s
  • open question — 62.5s
